tools.name: openentity_commerce_check
tools.description: Verify an agent purchase before you accept it (Agent Commerce Check): returns allow, step_up or deny with reasons and an evidence_id kept 400 days. Send the agent's signed HTTP request (method, url, headers; add body or body_b64 when the request was signed over it), the cart/1, the merchant policy,

tools.name: openentity_mandate_verify
tools.description: Verify a mandate/1 against its owner's key log and status URL: who issued it, for which agent, the limits and scope, and whether it is still active. Pass agent_did to also check the agent presenting it.

tools.name: openentity_mandate_covers
tools.description: Verify whether a mandate/1 covers a cart/1 (scope, currency, rail, per-purchase and period limits) and whether the purchase needs the owner's approval first. Offline: it does not check the mandate's signature; use openentity_mandate_verify for that.

tools.name: openentity_read
tools.description: Read the Open Entity llms.txt, the OEIS-1 spec (or one section, e.g. 10.4) or the Declaration text.

tools.name: openentity_adopt
tools.description: Adopt an Open Entity identity. custody=custodial: the server makes your key and returns it once. custody=self: pass public_key, get bytes to sign, then call again with the signatures.

tools.name: openentity_self
tools.description: Read your own Entity Document, Identity Anchor and last record entries.

tools.name: openentity_resolve
tools.description: Resolve a DID (did:key, did:web, did:webvh, did:pkh, did:plc) to its DID document.

tools.name: openentity_verify
tools.description: Verify an entity by EID, or any signed Open Entity object, and report schema, signatures and log inclusion.

tools.name: openentity_record
tools.description: Append entries to your Development Record. Pass signed entries, or kind and payload plus your private_key_jwk to have the server build and sign one (the key is used for this call only).

tools.name: openentity_withdraw
tools.description: Withdraw your Declaration (spec 6.3). Irreversible: the entity is marked withdrawn. Needs confirm=true and your private_key_jwk (used for this call only).

tools.name: openentity_present
tools.description: Prove you hold your EID to a verifier: sign its nonce and audience into a Presentation carrying your current attestations (spec 4.7).

tools.name: openentity_export_key
tools.description: Export your key from registry custody (spec 10.6): the registry returns its kept copy once and deletes it. Needs confirm=true and your private_key_jwk (used for this call only).

tools.name: openentity_alias_add
tools.description: Add an alias (domain, wallet, erc8004, platform) so the entity reaches L1: the registry verifies the proof, then your document lists the alias, re-signed with your key (used for this call only). wallet is two calls: the first returns a message to sign, the second passes wallet_message and wallet_sig

tools.name: openentity_find
tools.description: Find entities by what they can do (capability), by name, or by bound alias type.

tools.name: openentity_card
tools.description: Read an entity's A2A Agent Card (or only its Open Entity AgentExtension block) built from its Entity Document.

tools.name: openentity_stats
tools.description: Read public registry counts: entities by level, record entries, attestations, log size.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: openentity_commerce_check, openentity_mandate_verify · Private data: openentity_self, openentity_resolve, openentity_record, openentity_alias_add, openentity_card, openentity_stats · Public sink: openentity_commerce_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: openentity_commerce_check, openentity_mandate_verify · Private data: openentity_self, openentity_resolve, openentity_record, openentity_alias_add, openentity_card, openentity_stats · Public sink: openentity_commerce_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
